comparison: Both strongly support the structural determination and interface characterization (C6-C8, C38, C43-C51). Strong agreement on biochemical validation of CBC-ALYREF interaction (C30, C33, C56-C57, C61, C63-C65). Both recognize the mutagenesis data validates structural observations. OpenEval explicitly notes NCBP1 as major binding partner (C62-C65), while peer reviewers focus on the overall confirmation of the interface through biochemical assays.

Both address viral hijacking mechanism (C76-C77, C79-C80). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on structural overlays and in vivo data, acknowledging lack of direct functional validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the absence of cell-based studies to test the proposed viral hijacking mechanism. Key disagreement on sufficiency of structural evidence alone.

Perfect agreement on methodological choice to use mouse ALYREF2 (C31-C32). Both support this decision based on sequence conservation and functional equivalence. OpenEval provides detailed justification from purification behavior and sequence alignment, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by not questioning the approach.

Both rate cancer-associated mutations (C99-C101) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the speculative nature of functional claims ('could reduce') lacking experimental validation. Peer reviewers similarly emphasize absence of functional data to test whether mutations affect ALYREF binding and mRNA export in cellular contexts. Strong agreement on need for validation.

Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of functional studies in cells to test coordination models. Disagreement on whether structural data alone sufficiently supports mechanistic claims.

Both address flexibility and mechanistic models (C68, C72-C73). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are speculative models lacking direct experimental validation. Peer reviewers similarly note absence of functional data to support proposed models. Strong agreement that these represent hypotheses requiring validation.

Peer reviewers include this in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation about sequential binding and coordination models, emphasizing need for functional studies. Both recognize gap between structural and functional evidence.
